note: v3 of this file (re-measurement pass against the current 10-feature/depth=9 production model). feature_dimensionality, tree_depth, and register_granularity were re-run again on the CURRENT production feature set/model (superseding the v2 numbers below, which were measured against the prior 8-feature/depth=6 model). digest_payload_size moved out of not_run: the Tofino-throughput comparison remains genuinely infeasible and is NOT attempted, but a real, narrower, feasible substitute (real digest-transmission-latency vs real payload size, no hardware comparison) was run live and is included. bloom_deduplication and threshold_T are unchanged: both are live single-replay switch measurements independent of the model, not re-run. A new feature_importance section covers the 2 features that didn't exist in the v2 feature-dimensionality ablation.

feature_dimensionality.method: Real ablation, re-scoped for the current 10-feature production model (production hyperparameters max_depth=9, learning_rate=0.2 held fixed; only the feature set varies). Groups C/D isolate syn_noack_ratio's and ack_ratio's real INDIVIDUAL marginal contributions, which the original 2-features-at-once test folded into one combined delta.

results.feature_set: E: Basic (4): pkt_rate, byte_rate, port_div, tcp_flags

feature_dimensionality.finding: ack_ratio ALONE (D: F1=0.860) contributes almost as much as both new features combined (A: 0.861) -- it is the primary real driver, not an equal partner with syn_noack_ratio. syn_noack_ratio alone (C: 0.855) contributes less individually, despite ranking #1 by internal model gain (see feature_importance below) -- these are two different, non-contradictory real analyses: marginal single-feature addition to a smaller set vs. relative importance within the full model where both features can specialize/interact.

superseded_v2_8feature_result.note: Superseded (measured against the prior 8-feature/depth=6 model). Kept for historical comparison only.

results.feature_set: Basic (4 features: pkt_rate, byte_rate, port_div, tcp_flags)

feature_importance.method: Real XGBoost internal importance scores (gain/weight/cover) read directly from the trained production booster (controller/ml/model.json) via get_score(importance_type=...), all 10 real features -- did not exist for the prior 8-feature model.
feature_importance.finding: By gain (the standard 'how useful is this feature when used' metric), the two new features together account for over half of total real gain (50.3%), with syn_noack_ratio ranked #1 -- consistent with it being the single biggest real driver of the accuracy improvement. But by weight (how OFTEN a feature is used to split), syn_noack_ratio ranks LAST (1.2%) -- it's used in relatively few splits, but those splits are extremely high-value when it is used. Both are real and correct; they answer different questions.

tree_depth.method: Real ablation, re-run at max_depth in {3,6,9,12} on the CURRENT 10-feature production dataset (superseding the v2 result below, which used the prior 8-feature set).
tree_depth.finding: depth=9 is confirmed as the real best choice ON THE ACTUAL 10-feature production set (F1=0.861, beats both depth=6's 0.856 and depth=12's 0.859) -- validates the production hyperparameter with its own real ablation on the real current feature set, not carried over from a different ablation run on a different feature set.

superseded_v2_8feature_result.note: Superseded (measured against the prior 8-feature model, where depth=12 appeared best because syn_noack_ratio/ack_ratio didn't exist yet to give depth=9 enough signal to separate on). Kept for historical comparison only.

register_granularity.method: Two real measurements at each width: (a) crc32-via-string approximation (baseline_reimpl/common.py's documented stand-in), and (b) a REAL bit-exact CRC16 -- verified directly against BMv2's actual source (~/build/behavioral-model/src/bm_sim/calculations.cpp: poly=0x8005, init=0, refin/refout=true, xorout=0, i.e. standard CRC-16/ARC), applied to the real raw 4-byte big-endian on-wire IPv4 address (matching p4/p4_xgboost.p4's actual hash() call input exactly, not a decimal-string approximation). crcmod's config was independently verified against the published CRC-16/ARC check value (0xBB3D for ASCII '123456789') before use.

chernoff_bound_investigation.method: The thesis's own P(Spurious Trigger) formula (a single-hash binomial tail, matching the real single-register-array P4 implementation exactly -- see note below) was evaluated at the REAL observed attacker packet volume in this dataset (A=62,171,695 packets, computed exactly via scipy.stats.binom.sf, not approximated), and bisected to find what volume A would be needed to reproduce the thesis's claimed 3.8% figure.
chernoff_bound_investigation.ratio: 732x -- the real observed attack volume is ~732x larger than what the thesis's own formula requires to produce its claimed 3.8% figure
chernoff_bound_investigation.d1_check: The thesis formally defines CMS with min-aggregation over d>=2 rows, but the SPECIFIC P(Spurious Trigger) bound they derive and use is already a single-hash (d=1) binomial tail -- which matches the real P4 implementation exactly (one register array, one hash() call, no min-aggregation, confirmed by direct inspection of p4/p4_xgboost.p4). This was checked, not assumed: the d=1-vs-d>1 concern raised as a hypothesis does NOT explain the gap, since bound and implementation are consistently d=1.

register_granularity.finding: Three real, checked explanations, only one of which holds: (1) hash-function/encoding choice does NOT explain the gap -- the real bit-exact CRC16 gives a HIGHER collision rate (52.05% at w=1024) than the approximation (43.10%), not lower; if anything the approximation understated the real number. (2) the d=1-vs-multi-row CMS structural concern does NOT apply -- the thesis's own derived bound is already d=1-shaped, matching the real implementation. (3) REAL EXPLANATION: the thesis's claimed 3.8% figure is only mathematically consistent with a total attack volume ~732x smaller than what CIC-DDoS2019's real UDP+SYN flood actually contains. At the real observed volume, the thesis's own formula predicts P(Spurious Trigger)=1.0 (numerically indistinguishable from certainty) for any bucket shared with real attack traffic -- not a bug, but the bound correctly describing conditions far worse than the original (unfounded) 3.8% figure assumed. Separately, the 'collision_pct' metric this ablation measures (a static fraction of distinct IPs sharing a bucket) is not literally the same quantity as the thesis's dynamic per-flow P(Spurious Trigger); both point to the same real conclusion (the original 3.8% figure has no basis at real attack volumes) but are not numerically interchangeable, and should not be conflated in the thesis text.

bloom_deduplication.method: Real simple_switch log inspection: replayed the real 150-packet attacker trigger slice once, counted (a) how many packets crossed the CMS threshold (would each attempt a digest without dedup) vs (b) how many bloom_reg writes actually occurred (real digest-eligible events, i.e. with dedup as currently implemented).
bloom_deduplication.finding: Real ~50x reduction in digest volume from dedup on just this small 150-packet slice. Not re-run against the current model: this is a live single-replay switch measurement independent of the model, using the same fixed attacker_trigger_slice.pcap as before.

threshold_T.method: Real inter-arrival timestamps from the real 150-packet attacker trigger slice -- how long (real elapsed time) it actually took this real attacker to send T packets.
threshold_T.finding: MAJOR real divergence: at the thesis's own chosen T=100, this real attacker's actual packet rate takes ~23.75 SECONDS of real elapsed time to cross the threshold -- nowhere close to the thesis's implied ~28ms total end-to-end latency budget. Not re-run against the current model: this is a live single-replay switch measurement independent of the model.

digest_payload_size.method: The original ablation (28-byte vs 1500-byte digest 'pushing gRPC transmission latency from 10.2ms to 48ms') has NO real basis anywhere -- not in this rebuild, not verifiable in any prior real measurement; it is part of the same fabricated ablation set flagged since v1 of this rebuild, and the real control plane is Thrift/nanomsg, not gRPC, at all. Comparing real BMv2 throughput against a Tofino ASIC's >5,000 alerts/sec claim remains genuinely infeasible and was NOT attempted. A real, narrower, feasible substitute WAS run: 3 real P4 program variants (scripts/digest_payload_ablation.p4, compiled with different digest struct sizes -- p4c caps a single field at 2048 bits, so the ~1500-byte variant uses 6 padding fields, a real compiler constraint) were compiled and live-tested, measuring real wall-clock time from listener start to real digest receipt via the actual nanomsg notification socket (same real wire path controller/p4/digest_listener.py uses).
digest_payload_size.finding: Real payload size has NO measurable effect on real transmission+receipt latency across a 245x size increase (6 to 1470 bytes): 25745.6ms / 25744.9ms / 25759.8ms -- a ~15ms spread with no monotonic trend (the 100-byte variant is actually the FASTEST of the three). The ~25.7s figure in all three is almost entirely the real CMS threshold-crossing time (T=100, already independently measured at ~23.75s -- see threshold_T above), not digest transmission: once triggered, real local nanomsg IPC delivers a payload this size near-instantaneously regardless of size. This is a single real trial per variant, not a repeated series -- a real limitation, noted rather than smoothed over -- but the complete absence of a monotonic trend across 3 real trials spanning a 245x size range is itself informative.

not_run.digest_payload_size_vs_tofino_throughput: Requires comparing against real Tofino ASIC line-rate throughput (>5,000 alerts/sec claim in the thesis) -- BMv2 is a software reference switch and cannot faithfully reproduce Tofino performance, same reasoning baseline_reimpl/README.md already applies to excluding throughput/latency baseline comparisons. Dropped rather than faked with a software-switch number presented as if it were hardware-comparable. (The real, feasible substitute -- payload size vs real transmission latency, no Tofino comparison -- IS included above as digest_payload_size.)
